System tracking snapshot. Check again to update.

Tracked for this app counts background child processes with this app’s UID in the system records. Tracked device-wide counts all entries in the same active table, rather than all processes on the phone. The records can lag briefly and reflect the latest check.

The effective limit is shared by apps across the device. 32 is a common default since Android 12. 256 is an optional generous value: it does not create or preallocate 256 processes. Keep the default if operation is stable.

Missing, unrecognized, or inaccessible records display “—”, never an assumed zero. When monitoring is disabled, the limit may not be used for trimming.

Without root, start Shizuku using ADB on a computer. Start it again after rebooting. See the official Shizuku guide.

This differs from Background process limit in Developer options. Changes affect all apps and do not guarantee continued operation. Vendor cleanup, memory pressure, or system resets can still interrupt services. This app never changes the setting automatically.
This limit can be inspected on Android 12 and later.
Not checked. Authorize Shizuku to read the effective value.
Set the device-wide background child process limit to 256. Background programs may use more resources. You can restore the system default here later. Continue?
Remove the custom limit and let the system decide. The system may stop excess child processes that are currently running. Continue?
The configuration was written, but the observed effective limit is not 256. Check again; this system may not support the setting or may override it.

Manually exempts only this app from Android idle CPU and network restrictions. Some phones synchronize Unrestricted battery use to this same whitelist, so the two entries overlap; vendor background policies may still need separate configuration. Auto-start controls permission to launch automatically, while the child-process limit controls a count. The app already uses a foreground service and wake lock. Exemption cannot guarantee protection from vendor cleanup, memory pressure or child-process termination.
System confirmed: this app is exempt from battery optimization
System confirmed: battery optimization still applies to this app

Use Shizuku to add only this app to the system idle whitelist, then check the system state. This may increase battery use while the screen is off. You can remove it here. Device-wide power saving and other apps are unchanged. Continue?
Remove this app from the user idle whitelist. CPU and network access may be restricted while the screen is off. Built-in system exemptions are retained. Continue?
Whitelist saved. The system confirms this app is exempt from battery optimization.
User exemption removal confirmed. The status above can still show exempt if a built-in system exemption applies.
Could not confirm the whitelist change. Check again or use system battery optimization settings.
